title: Incident Triage Toolkit: templated recovery snippets + shadow-runner
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Oncall engineers frequently copy/paste ad-hoc remediation commands from long runbooks. That process is slow, error-prone, and hard to review. Complex incidents require stitching multiple small actions (check, restart, bump, reroute) and there is no low-friction way to validate a sequence against a service without touching production. We want a lightweight toolkit that makes recovery snippets first-class: small, parameterized, auditable actions that can be composed, simulated, and then executed with safety gates.
proposal: Deliver a "templated recovery snippet" catalog (idempotent micro-operations with typed inputs and example fixtures) plus a "shadow-runner" simulator that executes snippets against a sandboxed environment or synthetic telemetry to validate expected outcomes. Key capabilities: (1) snippet schema and parameter validation, (2) CLI + Console UI for searching and running snippets, (3) shadow/dry-run mode that returns a side-effects diff and confidence score, (4) RBAC and KMS-backed audit trail for live execution, (5) telemetry hooks so the suggestion engine can propose snippets during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Snippet catalog CRUD (create/update/delete) with JSON schema validation and example fixtures
CLI command to run a snippet in shadow mode that returns simulated side-effect summary within 10s for common snippets
Console integration: searchable catalog entry + run-in-shadow button + promote-to-live flow with permission check
Audit log entry per execution (shadow or live) with parameters, user, and outcome linkable to incident timeline
Telemetry metrics: time-to-suggestion, shadow-vs-live outcome divergence rate tracked in Metrics dashboard
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (MVP): support a small set of snippet types (service-restart, db-rollforward-check, scale-pool-adjust) implemented as idempotent HTTP operations against operator API
Sandbox strategy: start with in-cluster namespace clones + lightweight data fixtures vs full synthetic infra (cost trade-off) — we'll seed common failure modes
Security: require KMS envelope for any snippet marked 'destructive' and gate live execution behind admin role
Telemetry: attach a 'confidence' heuristic based on shadow-runner simulation result and historical runbook outcomes
Observability: emit structured events to Ops Console so incident timelines can link to simulation diffs and live run results
tradeoffs_and_risks: Simulation fidelity vs maintenance: high-fidelity sims reduce false positives but cost more to maintain and run; MVP will accept limited coverage

False confidence: a shadow-runner that misses a side-effect pattern could produce dangerous guidance — mitigate with conservative confidence scoring and mandatory human approval for destructive snippets
Operational cost: sandbox environments will incur infra costs; we'll pilot with a single critical-service sandbox and expand after measuring ROI
rollout_plan: Week 0-1: implement snippet schema + minimal catalog backend + CLI skeleton
Week 2: build shadow-runner adapter for 'service-restart' and 'scale-pool-adjust' snippets; integrate with synthetic fixture for core service A
Week 3: Console UI button + audit events; limited beta with Oncall team; collect metrics
Week 4: iterate on confidence scoring, add PM review feedback, prepare release notes and training runbook
Post-release: expand snippet types and add scheduled sandbox refresh, refine telemetry-driven suggestions
qa_and_validation: Manual scenario tests: 8 incident patterns run in shadow vs live against staging cluster
Automated regression: nightly smoke-run of all catalog snippets against sandbox fixtures
Oncall dogfood: enable beta for 2-week period, capture outcome deltas and operator feedback
notes: Decision: MVP will not attempt full DB failover simulation — instead capture pre/post checks and expected diffs
Design feedback from PM (Rowan): prefer explicit input examples per snippet to reduce mis-parameterization
Security review: pre-authorization required for any snippet that modifies persistent state; plan to onboard security early
